items.title: EPFO approves periodic PF payouts for retirees, eases withdrawal norms
points: The decisions were taken at the 240th meeting of the Central Board of Trustees (CBT), chaired by Labour Minister Mansukh Mandaviya in New Delhi.

BS-VI vehicles between six and 10 years old, of either kind, stay on a yearly certificate.
BS-VI vehicles more than 10 years old will also move to a six-month certificate.
A certificate renewed within 10 days before it expires will start from old one’s expiry date.

Here’s our guide to the best controller settings for GTA 6 on PS5 and Xbox.
Of course, these are part and parcel of the best beginner tips to play GTA 6, but we offer you an in-depth look at all of them.
Changing these controller and gameplay settings in GTA 6 can make your movement, driving, and gunplay feel sharper and smoother.
To access controller settings in GTA 6, head to the Pause Menu → Settings → Controller, and you’ll open the most expansive controller customization you’ve ever seen in a Rockstar title.
Choosing the right Aim Response Curve makes a bigger difference in GTA 6 than cranking up raw sensitivity.

items.title: US Sour Crude’s War Premium Vanishes as Supply Surges
points: The price of US sour oil has plunged, as a surge of oil from Venezuela, Canada and the Middle East gives refiners ample barrels to choose from.
Rising production of heavy-sour crude in Venezuela and Canada has pushed global prices lower in recent weeks.

US refiners, whose Gulf Coast and Midwest plants are major buyers of heavier oil, have benefited from the additional supplies from Canada and Latin America, while higher shipping costs are depressing the value of barrels at their origin because they’re…

“Incremental supply looks to be dominated by heavier and more sour barrels, especially out of Canada, Venezuela, and the Middle East,” Valero’s head of crude supply Randy Hawkins said in an October earnings call.
It’s a “race to the bottom” Phillips 66’s executive vice president of marketing and commercial Brian Mandell said on a call with analysts the same month.

items.title: Court in Keralam’s Kannur sentences man, paramour to imprisonment for 2017 murder
points: A trial court in Kannur sentenced a man and his paramour to life imprisonment and rigorous imprisonment along with a fine of ₹50,000 each in a 2017 murder case.
The Thalassery First Additional District and Sessions Court presided over by Judge C.J.
Denny pronounced the sentence on Thursday (November 19, 2026), a day after declaring both accused guilty.
The convicts are Jobby James of Peravur and Jancy Babu alias Annie Babu of Payyavoor and wife of the deceased.

In addition to the life sentence, the court awarded the first accused four years of additional imprisonment and imposed a separate fine of ₹50,000 under Section 449 of the Indian Penal Code for house trespass.
The court ordered that the fine amount, if recovered, be paid to the parents of the deceased, provided they are alive.
The court further ordered that each accused would have to undergo one additional year of imprisonment in default of payment of the respective fines.

items.title: ARC Adds Another U.S.-Flag Ro/Ro Ship to Strengthen Military Sealift Capacity
points: American Roll-On/Roll-Off Carrier Group (ARC) has added another large vehicle carrier to its U.S. -flag fleet, strengthening its ability to transport heavy military equipment and commercial cargo overseas.

The 757-foot ARC United (IMO 9505053) joins the fleet under the federal Maritime Security Program (MSP), which maintains commercially operated U.S. -flag ships available to support military sealift requirements during war and national emergencies.
The Large Car and Truck Carrier (LCTC) has 13 cargo decks, including five with hoistable sections, and capacity for nearly 8,000 car-equivalent units.
Its stern ramp can handle rolling loads of up to 320 metric tons, allowing the vessel to load and discharge heavy equipment without shoreside cranes.
The addition follows the September reflagging of ARC Freedom, another nearly 8,000-car-capacity vessel brought into the U.S. fleet.

“In my 32 years at sea, my vessels moved a lot of military cargo, and I saw firsthand how much our troops depend on American civilian merchant mariners to keep them supplied,” said Captain Willie Barrere, national president of American Maritime Officers.

items.title: FIR against two former Bengal Ministers over sexual assault charges
points: A First Information Report (FIR) has been lodged against two former Ministers in the West Bengal government, Indranil Sen and Bratya Basu, along with several senior government officials, over multiple charges, including sexual assault.

The FIR was lodged at Baguiati Police Station under the Bidhannagar Commissionerate by social activist Rajib Sarkar on behalf of multiple women who have either been artists or employed by the West Bengal Information and Cultural Affairs Department.
A zero FIR has been registered against 40 accused individuals, including the two former Ministers, he said.
Mr. Sen was arrested by the Kolkata Police on October 28, 2026, in connection with a Durga Puja ticket scam case by the Enforcement Directorate.
Five former Ministers, who had been part of Mamata Banerjee’s cabinet, have been arrested since the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) government came to power in May 2026.
The arrests of former ministers began with former state Fire Services Minister Sujit Bose.

items.title: Ex-servicemen, families stage protest in Keralam’s Kannur demanding better ECHS facilities
points: The protest was organised by the Kannur district committee of the Kerala State Ex-Servicemen’s League, highlighting the shortage of ECHS empanelled super-specialty hospitals in the district.
The organisation said thousands of ex-servicemen and their family members were facing serious difficulties in accessing quality medical treatment due to the inadequate number of empanelled hospitals.
The protest march began at 10 a.m. from the DSC Record office circle and was flagged off by league president Col.
The subsequent dharna in front of the Kannur head post office was inaugurated by T.O.
The committee’s demands included ensuring prompt disbursement of medical treatment bills to empanelled hospitals.
The organisation also sought to establish an ECHS polyclinic at Alakode, Taliparamba, and Thalassery.

The two areas lie approximately 150 to 240 miles east of Pago Pago, in waters ranging from 4,630 to 20,100 feet deep.
The $6 million in combined high bids matched the minimum asking price of $3 million for each area.

items.title: Devotees visiting Guruvayur temple must be treated with respect, says Kerala High Court
points: The Kerala High Court has held that every devotee visiting the Guruvayur Sree Krishna Temple ought to be cared for and treated with respect.
Temple employees at every level must act with the highest degree of equanimity and must not lose their temper with any devotee.
Every devotee would like to spend as much time as possible in front of the deity, and employees must ensure that the queue moves, with hundreds of others waiting for darshan.
It thus requires a fine balance between rival interests.
Whatever be the reason or provocation, an altercation or bad behaviour on the part of any employee cannot be tolerated, the High Court said.
The standing counsel for the Guruvayur Devaswom Board intervened to say that there were instances when some devotees unfairly created provocation, leading, in one case, to a stabbing incident.

items.title: Four-year-old dies in accident at plywood manufacturing unit in Keralam’s Perumbavoor
points: In a tragic incident, the four-year-old son of a migrant worker couple died after getting trapped in the dryer belt at a plywood manufacturing unit in Thandekkad near Perumbavoor on Thursday (November 19, 2026) evening.
The deceased was identified as Meraj Sheikh, son of Noor Jamal Sheikh and Noorima Khatun, natives of West Bengal.
Noor Jamal Sheikh is an employee of the company.
The child who had gone to the factory along with his mother reportedly got trapped in the belt of a veneer-drying machine while playing.
The seriously injured child died on the spot.
Three years ago, a four-year-old girl had drowned in a wastewater pit at a plywood manufacturing unit at Allapra in Kuttipadam near Perumbavoor.
In that case also, the child had accompanied her mother who was working in the unit.

The Kerala State Human Rights Commission had registered a suo moto case and directed the District Police Chief (Ernakulam Rural) and the District Labour Officer to submit a detailed report on the incident.

items.title: India, Bangladesh staring at Ganga water pact expiry amid strained ties
points: India and Bangladesh are facing the stark possibility of the lapse of the three-decade Ganga Water Treaty early next month, barring an intervention by the top political leadership of the two sides, as formal talks for its renewal are yet to begin, people…

The people pointed out that India and Bangladesh had agreed to form a joint technical committee to initiate discussions for renewing the Ganga Waters Treaty when former premier Sheikh Hasina made her last visit to India in June 2024, weeks before she was…
The letter said Bangladesh had completed its preparations and expressed the hope that India will begin formal negotiations before the pact expires on December 12, they said.

items.title: NHAI offers tea, washing kit to drivers at toll plazas on Chennai – Bengaluru Highway to prevent accidents
points: NHAI officials said that vehicles from Chennai and Bengaluru were stopped at toll plazas in Pallikonda and Vaniyambadi.
Patrol staff serve a cup of tea and a few biscuits to drivers between 4 a.m and 6 a.m every day.
“It is an essential break for drivers, especially in the wee hours when they tend to doze off.
The drivers are also provided with safety lessons on driving,” said Sarath Patel, Route Patrol Officer (RPO), NHAI.
NHAI officials said that the initiative was aimed at bringing down road accidents on the busy stretch, adding that most of the accidents occur between 2 a.m. to 5 p.m.
Apart from serving tea and biscuits at the toll plaza, drivers are also provided a small kit that contained a toothpaste, brush, water bottle, and a towel before they were allowed to proceed.

items.title: What brews for Indian Coffee House?
points: Seating himself at one of the unoccupied brick benches built into the structure, he opens a newspaper over a brick-made table.
As he pores over the day’s news in the light streaming through the jaalis, a bearer wearing a green-lined white headgear places a cup of coffee and reddish-brown cutlet on his table.

This scene, which plays out almost with the grace of a classic film sequence, might look anachronistic in these times, just like how the coffee house building itself looks when compared to the world around it.
Global coffee house chains, numerous trendy newage cafes and restaurants offering a whole new variety of dishes have come up in the past few years in Keralam, just like in the other States.
But the Indian Coffee House seems stuck in a time warp.

items.title: Report links cloud-seeding to AQI gain in Delhi; but western disturbance may have had a role
points: Light rain fell at a few places in Delhi and pollution readings dropped the morning after a cloud-seeding sortie on November 14, according to a post-flight report by the firm that carried out the operation.

The report, prepared by Bengaluru-based Kyathi Climate Modification Consultants LLP (KCMC), hired by the Delhi government and seen by HT, says a Super King Air B200 aircraft took off from Delhi at 2.53pm and returned at 5.03pm.
Between 3.11pm and 4.26pm it released seeding material eight times over seven locations in Delhi-NCR: Siraspur, Bankner in Bawana, Sersa (twice), Baghpat, Burari, Loni Road and Sonia Vihar.
On air quality, the report said Bawana’s AQI fell from 406 at 3pm on November 14, shortly before the aircraft released material over Bankner, to 362 at 10am on November 15.

The gauge at IGNOU recorded 1mm between 3.45am and 7.30am on November 15, which matches the report’s figure for the campus, and the one at Karni Singh Shooting Range recorded 1mm between 4am and 4.30am.

items.title: 3 killed as minibus plunges into 100-foot gorge on Kodaikanal-Palani Ghat Road

The passengers were returning from a wedding function in Kodaikanal.
Rescue teams rushed to the spot and shifted the injured to nearby hospitals.
